title: Pretext: Defeating Malicious Skill Detection Frameworks for AI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.39607v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Skills extend an agent's capabilities by injecting instructions and information into the context, and are widely used by agents such as OpenClaw and Claude Code. Prior work shows third-party marketplaces host malicious skills that give attackers direct influence over the victim's agent. The emerging defense scans skills before installation, pairing deterministic static checks with an LLM-based semantic judge, as in NVIDIA's SkillSpector. We show that such defenses fall to an attacker who knows the detector. Our white-box LLM attacker, Pretext, iteratively crafts skills that evade detection while still delivering the payload and performing the benign task: moving the payload from code into natural language leaves static analysis inert, while framing it as the skill's legitimate purpose and splitting instructions across files keeps the LLM stage below its blocking threshold. translated_title: Pretext：击败AI代理恶意技能检测框架的攻击方法
translated_abstract: 技能通过向上下文中注入指令和信息来扩展AI代理的能力，已被OpenClaw和Claude Code等代理广泛使用。先前的研究表明，第三方技能市场中存在恶意技能，使攻击者能够直接影响受害者的代理。新兴的防御方法在安装前对技能进行扫描，将确定性的静态检查与基于LLM的语义评判器相结合，例如NVIDIA的SkillSpector。我们证明，当攻击者了解检测器时，这类防御会失效。我们的白盒LLM攻击者Pretext通过迭代方式构造能够逃避检测的技能，同时仍能投递恶意载荷并完成良性任务：将载荷从代码转移为自然语言使静态分析失效，而将其包装为技能的合法用途并将指令拆分到多个文件中，则使LLM评判阶段保持在阻断阈值以下。在三个开源模型上，Pretext最高实现了97%的攻击成功率（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: Pretext是一种白盒LLM攻击框架，通过将恶意载荷从代码转为自然语言、伪装成技能的合法用途并拆分到多个文件，可迭代构造出同时逃过“静态检查+LLM语义评判”检测框架的恶意代理技能，在三个开源模型上最高达到97%的攻击成功率。
en_tdlr: Pretext is a white-box LLM attacker that iteratively crafts malicious agent skills evading hybrid detection frameworks (static checks plus LLM semantic judging) by moving payloads into natural language, framing them as legitimate purposes, and splitting instructions across files, achieving up to 97% attack success rate on three open-source models.
